title: Astrid and the Regiment
premise: In 1917, Freya Montrose keeps a secret ledger of soldiers' real names and last words — the ones the officers' reports erase — while her brother Anders serves as a clerk who requisitions her coastal town for the war effort. When the army seizes the town, the ledger is confiscated as evidence of 'subversive record-keeping,' forcing Freya to trade truths with the very officers she has been quietly contradicting. As a hospital ship prepares to sail on the morning tide with one berth left, Freya must choose between her wounded brother, a deserter whose name exists only in her ledger, and the truth itself. In the end, she gives the berth to the deserter, surrenders the ledger's pages to be burned, and discovers that memory survives not in records but in the people who carry names forward — including her own, finally spoken aloud by those she saved.
about_author: Petra Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing field hospital records from the First World War before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse on the Baltic coast, where the tide still dictates the rhythm of her mornings.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Freya, POV: introduces the ledger hidden beneath floorboards, recording names officers omit from casualty reports. Her routine at the converted schoolhouse hospital establishes the town's fragile normalcy. Emotional beat: quiet defiance — Freya believes remembering is a form of loyalty no order can revoke.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Anders, POV: arrives as army clerk to requisition the town — homes, church, and eventually the hospital itself. Brother meets sister across a bureaucratic table; he warns her that 'unauthorized records' will be seized. Emotional beat: dread and estrangement, family divided by uniform.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Freya, POV: a botched advance floods the ward; she records a dying private's true account, which contradicts the official report read aloud by Captain Ellery. Ellery suspects a leak. Emotional beat: the first open collision between her ledger and the army's version of events.

chapters.title: The Deserter in the Dunes
chapters.summary: Freya, POV: shelters Tomas, a shell-shocked soldier who deserted after his entire company was written off as 'expended.' His name exists nowhere but her ledger. She hides him as search parties sweep the dunes. Emotional beat: fear braided with fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Confiscation
chapters.summary: Anders, POV: ordered to search his sister's quarters, he finds the ledger — and hides it instead, forging an inventory. But Captain Ellery grows suspicious of the missing pages. Emotional beat: Anders torn between duty and blood, choosing blood for the first time.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs: Ellery interrogates Freya over the 'lost' ledger while Anders falsifies transport manifests upstairs. Freya realizes the ship arriving Friday carries wounded men — and only one unclaimed berth remains. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension; every answer is a negotiation.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Berth
chapters.summary: Freya, POV: Anders is injured in a supply-yard accident and needs evacuation; Tomas faces a firing squad if found; a dying nurse, Marta, begs for passage home. The arithmetic of love becomes unbearable. Emotional beat: rising crisis — the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs: at dawn, Freya puts Tomas aboard under a dead man's name from her ledger, stays with Anders through his fever, and sits with Marta as she dies ashore. Ellery nearly catches them at the gangplank. Emotional beat: sacrifice, terror, and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Ashes and Ink
chapters.summary: Freya, POV: to shield Anders, she surrenders the ledger and watches it burn in the requisitioned churchyard — then recites its contents from memory to a roomful of survivors' families. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into testimony; the theme of memory made flesh.

chapters.title: Carried
chapters.summary: Resolution, Freya and Anders, shared POV: the army withdraws; the town empties of uniforms. A letter arrives from Tomas, alive under his new name, signing himself with the words Freya once recorded. Brother and sister rebuild the schoolhouse together. Emotional beat: belonging redefined — family is whoever carries your name forward.
